title: Air India and Standard Chartered Launch Travel Wealth Offer for Global Indians
excerpt: Eligible Standard Chartered affluent clients in Singapore and the UAE will be offered Maharaja Club Gold or Silver status, while Air India customers gain access to dedicated cross-border wealth management.
body:
• Air India and Standard Chartered have announced a first-of-its-kind partnership linking the bank's cross-border wealth services with Air India's Maharaja Club loyalty programme.
  • Eligible affluent Global Indian clients in Singapore and the UAE will be offered Maharaja Club Gold or Silver status in the coming weeks, with extra baggage, priority check-in and boarding, lounge access, upgrade vouchers and bonus points.
  • Gold status also brings Star Alliance Gold, including access to more than 1,000 airport lounges worldwide across Air India and 25 other Star Alliance airlines.
  • Reader takeaway: if you bank with Standard Chartered in the UAE or Singapore and fly Air India, check eligibility when the proposition opens in the coming weeks - status is offered to eligible clients, not to all account holders.

Air India and Standard Chartered have announced a partnership that combines the bank's international banking and cross-border wealth capabilities with Air India's Maharaja Club loyalty programme for clients in Singapore and the UAE. The proposition will be available in the coming weeks, according to announcements reported by Chennai Vision and TradeArabia.

The two companies describe the deal as a first-of-its-kind travel and wealth proposition aimed at Global Indians whose lives, business and finances span borders. It works in both directions: bank clients gain airline status, and airline customers gain access to wealth services.

What Bank Clients Get on Air India

Standard Chartered will offer Maharaja Club Gold or Silver status to eligible affluent Global Indian clients in Singapore and the UAE. Maharaja Club status includes extra baggage allowance, priority check-in and boarding, airport lounge access, upgrade vouchers and bonus Maharaja Points, with benefits increasing from Silver to Gold.

Gold members also receive Star Alliance Gold status on eligible Air India journeys. That provides access to more than 1,000 airport lounges worldwide, priority airport services and extra baggage benefits, with recognition across 25 other Star Alliance member airlines in addition to Air India. Benefits on eligible journeys also include complimentary seat selection and applicable fee waivers, subject to programme terms.

"This partnership brings together two trusted heritage brands to create a distinctive proposition for Global Indians, whose lives, business and ambitions increasingly span borders."

— Rajesh Kannan, Head, Wealth and Retail Banking, UAE & Jersey, and Head, Global Indian Clients, Standard Chartered

What Air India Customers Get From the Bank

Eligible Air India customers banking with Standard Chartered in the UAE or Singapore will receive dedicated relationship management support, market outlook insights from the bank's Chief Investment Office, invitations to exclusive thought leadership events and tailored wealth solutions for cross-border financial needs. The offer is aimed at affluent clients, not mass-market account holders, and eligibility criteria will determine who qualifies in each market.

Nipun Aggarwal, Chief Commercial Officer at Air India, said the partnership expands Maharaja Club across key international markets and offers customers immediate access to premium status and global recognition. He linked the move to Air India's transformation into a world-class global airline and to deepening engagement with the global Indian community.

Context: Maharaja Club After the 2024 Redesign

Maharaja Club was redesigned in 2024 with a simplified structure, renamed tiers and an updated identity, and has since added millions of new members, according to the announcement. Members can earn and redeem Maharaja Points on Air India and Air India Express flights to and from 104 destinations across North America, Europe including the UK, Australia, the Middle East, Africa, Southeast Asia and South Asia, as well as on 25 other Star Alliance airlines. Partnerships with more than 100 brands across hospitality, retail, lifestyle and financial services also allow members to earn points on everyday spending. The Standard Chartered link adds banking as a direct route into elite status for two of the largest NRI hubs.

What It Means for Travellers in the UAE and Singapore

For Indian professionals and families based in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Singapore who fly home frequently, instant Gold or Silver status removes the usual mileage threshold for lounge access, extra baggage and priority handling on India routes. The practical step is to wait for the launch in the coming weeks and check eligibility through Standard Chartered in your market of residence. Status benefits vary by tier and by journey eligibility, so travellers should confirm baggage, lounge and upgrade terms before relying on them for a specific booking.

What's Next

Neither company gave an exact launch date beyond "the coming weeks" or published full eligibility thresholds in the announcement. Travellers and bank clients in Singapore and the UAE should watch for the eligibility notice from Standard Chartered and for Maharaja Club enrolment details from Air India. Further markets have not been announced.
